title: Trailing backslash inside a comment on the previous line is misread as a line continuation, skipping a valid top-level connect
description: _has_backslash_continuation_before tests `previous_line.rstrip().endswith('\\')` on the raw text of the previous physical line. A backslash at the end of a comment (e.g. `# see foo \`) or inside a string is NOT a Python line continuation, but this check treats it as one. _is_top_level_statement_anchor returns False when this helper is True (line 181), so a genuine module-level `pipeline.connect(...)` on the following line would be classified as a non-top-level continuation and skipped by _iter_connect_anchor_matches, silently dropping that edge. The helper inspects raw line text rather than code positions (it does not strip comments/strings the way the rest of the module's scanners do), which is the root inconsistency.
evidence: _has_backslash_continuation_before:152 builds previous_line from raw source and returns `.rstrip().endswith('\\')`; _is_top_level_statement_anchor:181 `if wrapper_depth < 0 or _has_backslash_continuation_before(...): return False`. Unlike _skip_string_literal-based scanners elsewhere, no comment/string awareness is applied to the previous line.
